Abstract.AbstractText: The incidence of metabolic disorders like type 2 diabetes and obesity continue to increase. In addition to the well-known contributors such as food intake and sedentary lifestyle, recent research in the exposure science discipline provides new evidence that exposure to endocrine disrupting chemicals like bisphenol A and phthalates via multiple routes (food, drink and skin contact) also contribute to the increased risk of metabolic disorders. Endocrine disrupting chemicals (EDCs) can disrupt any aspect of hormone action. It is becoming increasingly clear that EDCs not only affect endocrine function, but also adversely impact immune system function. In this review, we focus on human, animal and in vitro studies, which demonstrate that EDC exposure induces dysfunction of the immune system, which in turn has detrimental effects on metabolic health. Thus highlighting how the immune system is emerging as a novel player by which EDCs may mediate their effects on metabolic health. We also discuss studies highlighting novel mechanisms by which EDCs affect the immune system- these include receptor-mediated changes, effects on the microbiome, oxidative stress, and circadian disruption. Finally, we consider that a better understanding of the immunomodulatory roles of EDCs will provide clues to enhance the metabolic function, and contribute towards the long-term goal of reducing the burden of environment induced diabetes and obesity.
